correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the full product-group argument. With unnormalized Fourier transform using the positive exponential, conjugate values on opposite sites give 1+2 Σ Re(a_j ζ_j^{k_j}). All coordinates minimize independently, so positive definiteness is exactly Q=Σ q_{n_j}(a_j)≤1/2. The deficit is (1−2Q)/c+(2/c)Σ(q_n(a)−c Re a). For odd n=m, the two roots closest to −1 give q_m(u+iv)≥cu+s|v|, with equality to cu exactly on the nonnegative real ray. For n≠m in the odd-factor regime, q_n(a)−c Re a is the translated root polygon's support in direction (u,−v). Its half-plane offsets are cos(π/n)−c ν_x for the outward unit normals ν. The smallest offset, attained in a nearest-normal direction, equals cos(π/n)−c for n odd or (1−c)cos(π/n) for n even. These are positive. In the all-even regime q_n≥u, with equality precisely in the normal wedge at the rightmost vertex: u≥0 and |v|≤u tan(π/n). Equality in the sum gives the stated simplex in each case; the nonnegative weights of the even vertices are determined uniquely by (u_j,v_j). Zero characters require Q=1/2 and a minimum in every active coordinate. There are two residues per active odd coordinate; an even coordinate has its antipodal residue plus, at a wedge boundary, the previous residue for v>0 or the next for v<0. For sharp leakage constants the perturbed coordinate uses the corresponding nearest normal while the original real active coefficient is reduced to keep Q=1/2. For the imaginary constant, the repair corrects the false assertion that both minimizing residues stay minimizing. The strict gap to all other residues persists locally, so the pair still contains the minimum, and for v≠0 only one attains it. Thus q_m=cu+s|v| there; at u=(1/2−s|v|)/c this gives exact sharpness with just that coordinate occupied. This is an analytic all-orders argument, including n=3 and single-factor groups.
residual_risks: Finite floating-point examples are corroboration only. Fourier-zero counts refer to optimizers; sharp stability is asserted only when there is an odd order.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A scalar bound or optimization representation does not determine which mixed-order coordinates can carry complex mass, nor the exact tangent deficit constants. No inspected stronger theorem establishes those assertions for product stars.

evidence: General positivity and theta formulations give access to Fourier minimization, and periodic interval and root-support problems give other explicit examples. The present proof identifies the face using equality in independent regular-polygon supports and obtains the sharp constants from the minimum translated half-plane offsets.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These steps compute the equality and stability structure, not just the already available general optimization variables. The root-support matches cannot be substituted for a coordinate star because additional roots couple coordinates and change the minima.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The scalar optimum is not assessed as a standalone novelty. Equivalence of objectives under real symmetrization does not imply equivalence of the two sets of optimizers, as the nonreal even vertices demonstrate.

evidence: The five-point cross is the same support shape in two dimensions but the matched Fourier-moment problem optimizes an L⁶ moment. Indexed parity locking and hexagonal optimizer faces use A₃ or A₂ root supports. The separated five-site cyclic finding treats {0,±1,±3}, not the Cartesian coordinate star.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Identical sparsity shape or a parity-dependent face alone is not equivalent coverage; the objective, group and support constraints determine distinct feasible faces. None of those findings gives the mixed-order simplices and sharp coefficientwise deficit here.

originality.rationale: Pass for the precise mixed-order complex optimizer and sharp stability classification, not the scalar Turán bound in isolation. Prior finite-group results give the variational framework and one-coordinate analogues. The closest indexed optimizer findings change the support, group or objective; none of the inspected actual statements covers the complex simplices, Fourier-zero description and coefficientwise sharp deficit in this problem. The repair corrects the proof without changing the statement.

A cited older continuous-domain hexagon result was not relied on; neither access limits nor the support difference alone certify global priority.

DeCorte–de Laat–Vallentin variational formulation for context
value.rationale: The coordinate star is the intrinsic nearest-neighbor support of a product of cycles. The result shows how parity changes the full complex equality set, gives the exact transform zeros (hence the ranks for the associated circulant positive semidefinite kernels), and quantifies with sharp constants the penalty for imaginary or off-minimum-order mass. These are structural and perturbative facts not supplied by the scalar value alone.
residual_risks: Only nearest-neighbor support on a direct product is covered. No sharp all-even stability theorem is established.
